title: SLO-aware progressive rollout controller with environment overrides
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Goal: Build a progressive rollout controller that uses live SLO signals (latency P95, error rate, token cost anomalies) to automatically manage canaries, A/B comparisons, shadow runs, and automated rollback across Hosted, Dedicated and Private environments. The controller must expose a declarative rollout policy with environment-specific overrides and enforce safe guards for capacity-constrained Dedicated pools and air-gapped Private deployments.

Scope and requirements:
- Declarative policy model: phases (percentage or absolute sessions), metrics to watch, thresholds, duration, and rollback actions. Policies are defined in the same schema across environments but allow 'overrides' for env constraints.
- SLO-driven transitions: promote to next phase only if configured SLOs remain within thresholds for the full phase window. Immediate rollback on critical threshold breaches.
- Traffic modulation: support traffic ramp steps (e.g., 1%, 5%, 20%, 50%, 100%) and time-based or metric-based advances. Support both weighted routing and sticky session routing for chat use-cases.
- A/B evaluation harness: collect per-variant metrics, compute statistical significance for user-facing metrics (latency, safety/regression flags, perplexity proxy), and report with a confidence score in Console.
- Shadow runs: allow routing of copies of requests to new model variant for telemetry without affecting responses. Must be opt-in per-route and safe for Private envs (no external telemetry egress).
- Environment constraints: Hosted can do short windows and high sample rates; Dedicated cannot exceed reserved capacity and must support a guard that limits canary CPU/GPU share (defaults: 10% of pool for 24h unless escalated via manual approval). Private deployments may not have access to Redwood-hosted metrics; controller must support running locally with a metrics shim or a pull model for logs/metrics.
- Auto-rollback rules: configurable severity levels (soft rollback: reduce traffic; hard rollback: full cutover to previous stable model). Default hard rollback triggers: error_rate >= 0.5% sustained for 5 minutes OR P95 latency > 250ms increase vs baseline for 5 minutes.
- Observability: expose rollout timeline, per-phase metric graphs, diff view for A/B candidate vs baseline, audit trail (who approved, when), and links to traces/PRs.

Non-goals:
- Not implementing new model evaluation metrics (we'll surface existing eval signals). Not solving model training lifecycle.

Acceptance criteria:
1) Declarative policy schema implemented and validated by unit tests.
2) Controller can execute a 5-phase rollout in Hosted with SLO gating and automated rollback for test scenarios injected by chaos tests.
3) Dedicated pool constraint enforcement prevents canary from exceeding configured percentage; validated on staging Dedicated.
4) Private deployable controller can run in air-gapped mode: uses local metrics shim and requires no external telemetry by default.
5) Console surfaces rollout status, per-phase metrics, and a one-click abort.

Implementation notes / plan:
- Week 1: finalize schema and PRD, add feature flags and basic scheduler.
- Week 2: implement SLO evaluation engine and metric adapters (Prometheus for Hosted/Dedicated, local shim for Private).
- Week 3: integrate routing hooks + traffic modulation for the runtime, add shadowing pipelines.
- Week 4: add A/B stats engine, integrate Console views and audit logs, end-to-end tests and chaos scenarios.

Risks and mitigations:
- Metrics availability in Private: mitigate with a lightweight local agent and a CLI uploader; document export/ingest patterns for customers.
- Capacity explosion in Dedicated: default conservative caps and require manual approval for larger canaries; add quota checks at admission time.
- False-positive rollbacks due to noisy metrics: support rolling window smoothing and require multiple metric signals before hard rollback.

Open decisions:
- Final default thresholds for rollback (proposal in PRD, may be tuned after canary experiments).
- Whether to allow cross-tenant shadowing in Hosted for certain telemetry (privacy concerns).
